pr.title: Count and collapse review requests apart from your own pull requests
pr.head: d5a23b468fa60f15e19070c222ecb93a136dd7f2

summary: Projector's panel is the list above the Claude Code prompt that shows each open pull request the session fixes or reviews, one line each, under a header that counts them. Before this change the header gave one number, such as 24 pull requests, and clicking it collapsed the whole list. A session that reviews a busy repository could not tell how much of that list was its own work, and collapsing the list hid your pull requests along with everyone else's.

The change splits the list into two sections by author. Your own pull requests come first. Every pull request someone else wrote, a deleted account's included, is a review request. The header counts the two apart, as 14 pull requests · 10 review requests, and each count collapses only its own section to a + line.

Nothing new comes from GitHub. The watch daemon's query, and what each row shows, stay as they were. The review found the code clean; its one finding, about line wrapping in docs/plugins.md, is fixed at this head.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Operator: the account gh is signed in as, which the panel reads from the daemon's daemon.json. The code calls it the viewer.
  • Review request: a pull request someone other than the operator wrote. The panel decides this by author alone, not by GitHub's list of requested reviewers.
  • Section: something the header counts and can collapse: your pull requests (pr), the review requests (review), or a kind of inbox item.
  • Loading row: a pull request the daemon has not queried yet, so its author is unknown.

cards.html:

groups.title: Two sections of pull requests
groups.kicker: One test sorts each row, and the header, the rows, and the collapsed lines all read it
intro: The panel used to sort rows with isOwn, which put your pull requests first and everyone else's after them, grouped by author. The change replaces it with isReviewRequest, which answers the opposite question, and bySection, which returns the two sections as separate lists instead of one sorted list.

The header now has one count per section, and each count is its own button. A collapsed section of pull requests becomes a + line whose numbers work as tabs: clicking one opens that pull request's drawer, the panel of details under a row, beneath the collapsed line. Because both sections render through the same expander, that behavior is the same for either section.

checks.text: Every place that tells your rows from others' now reads isReviewRequest or the lists from bySection: the header counts, the author column's width, the author cell on each row, the collapsed lines, and the expanded list. So a row's author cell appears exactly on review requests. Checked by reading every caller at the head.

files.note: The classification, the split header, and the per-section collapsed lines.

checks.text: A loading row counts as yours, and moves to the review requests once its author arrives and turns out to be someone else. Before the operator is known, every row counts as yours, so no row shows an author column then.

The collapsed line and the expanded rows read the same section's list, so a pull request appears in one place only, and a drawer open under a collapsed section draws under that section's line and nowhere else. Checked by reading expander and the final render, and by the new test.
A section with no rows has no count in the header, and isCollapsed requires a count, so an empty section draws no + line even when it was left collapsed.

files.note: Adds review to Section, the type the stored list of collapsed sections holds.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: A new test for the split, and the existing header expectations updated
intro: The fixture's default pull request now names the operator as its author. Before, the default named no author, so the panel treated those rows as someone else's, though most tests meant them as yours. Under the new rule a missing author means a deleted account, so the default had to name the operator. A new fixture, p17, has no author, as GitHub reports a deleted account's pull request.

checks.text: This assertion is what catches a deleted account's pull request counted as yours: the header would read 3 pull requests · 3 review requests instead.
